question: Should CodexBar accept a LongCat provider that reads and forwards the full longcat.chat cookie header to undocumented private console endpoints, and if so should this current-base PR replace the conflict-blocked earlier PR?
rationale: The implementation cannot mechanically identify a narrower authentication cookie, and choosing between the proof-positive but conflict-blocked original branch and this newer branch is a repository ownership decision rather than a code-only repair.

options.title: Adopt this guarded replacement
options.body: Accept the full-cookie boundary, require redacted proof from this exact head, preserve original authorship, land this current-base branch, and close the earlier PR afterward.

options.title: Repair the original branch
options.body: Rebase and resolve https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/1697 so its established proof and discussion remain the canonical landing path, then close this duplicate branch.

options.title: Wait for supported authentication
options.body: Pause both implementations until LongCat exposes a documented usage API or a narrower supported authentication credential.

recommendation.title: Adopt this guarded replacement
recommendation.body: Accept the full-cookie boundary, require redacted proof from this exact head, preserve original authorship, land this current-base branch, and close the earlier PR afterward.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner has the strongest history on the shared provider and cookie-auth framework and is the appropriate decision owner for accepting a new credential boundary and selecting the canonical PR.
